title: U.S. House · New York's 4th Congressional District
area: Central Nassau County on Long Island, including most of the Town of Hempstead outside New York City.

context.text: This seat has flipped party control in each of the last three elections: Democrat Kathleen Rice did not seek re-election in 2022, when Republican Anthony D'Esposito won; Democrat Laura Gillen defeated D'Esposito in 2024, 51.1% to 48.8%. D'Esposito did not run for re-election in 2026. Jeanine Driscoll won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary over Marvin Suber Williams, 90.8% to 8.9%; Gillen's Democratic primary was canceled after five other Democrats withdrew or were disqualified.

As of September 2026, election forecasters rated the general election competitive: Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Lean Democratic," Decision Desk rated it "Likely Democratic," and Inside Elections rated it "Tilt Democratic." Registered Democrats outnumber Republicans in the district, which The New York Times described as a seat Republicans had viewed as a rare pickup opportunity.
A Libertarian Party candidate, Blay Tarnoff, is also on the November general-election ballot.

summary.text: Laura Gillen is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 4th Congressional District. A Nassau County attorney, she served as Hempstead Town Supervisor from 2018 to 2020, lost the 2022 race for this seat, and won it in 2024. She serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born July 10, 1969, in Rockville Centre, New York, and grew up in Baldwin; her House biography describes her as a Baldwin native.
Graduated from Sacred Heart Academy, then earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from Georgetown University (1991), where she was a George Baker Scholar.
After college she volunteered during the AIDS crisis and at Mother Teresa's Home for the Dying in Kolkata, according to her House biography.
Earned a J.D. from New York University School of Law (2000).

Worked as a litigator at Cahill Gordon & Reindel, including pro bono work representing victims of domestic violence, and from 2005 at the Nassau County firm Westerman Ball Ederer Miller Zucker & Sharfstein.
Elected Hempstead Town Supervisor in 2017, becoming the first Democrat in over a century to hold the office, and served from 2018 to 2020; she lost her 2019 re-election bid to Donald X. Clavin Jr.
Ran for NY-4 in 2022, winning the Democratic primary but losing the general election to Anthony D'Esposito; defeated D'Esposito in the 2024 rematch and was sworn in January 3, 2025.
Committee assignments are Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) and Science, Space, and Technology.
According to her House biography, she lives with her family in Rockville Centre.

priorities.text: Campaign material says she has focused on lowering costs, eliminating the SALT deduction cap, and securing federal funding for public safety, clean water, and family and student resources in Nassau County.
priorities.quote: Since taking office, Laura has proudly secured over $50M in federal funding to Nassau County, including direct investments in public safety, clean water and resources for families and students.

priorities.text: On immigration, says she has worked to extend Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitian immigrants in Nassau County.
priorities.quote: She has led the charge in Congress to extend TPS for law-abiding Haitians in Nassau County and across the country.

positions.summary: Has pushed to eliminate the federal SALT (state and local tax) deduction cap, which would reduce federal tax liability for higher-income Long Island homeowners.
Says she is fighting to extend tax credits that help families afford health insurance and has opposed Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: She has stood up against historic Medicaid cuts and helped pass reforms to crack down on insurance middlemen who are unfairly raising the cost of prescriptions.

record.text: Serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) and the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Space and Aeronautics subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Jeanine Driscoll
candidates.currentRole: Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes (since 2020)

summary.text: Jeanine Driscoll is the Hempstead Town Receiver of Taxes and the Republican nominee for NY-4. An attorney for over 30 years, she was an associate village justice in Bellerose before winning town-wide office in 2019. Her campaign says she is running to restore the full State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction and lower the tax burden.

background.text: Lives in Bellerose, Nassau County, according to News 12.
Earned a B.A. in American government and politics from The Catholic University of America and a J.D. from Fordham University.
Worked as an attorney for more than 30 years before holding elected office.
Served as an Associate Justice for the Village of Bellerose from 2015 to 2019.
Elected Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes in 2019 (taking office in 2020) and re-elected in 2023.
According to her campaign website, as Receiver of Taxes she has helped homeowners with exemptions and lower assessments, and she serves over 95% of the 4th District.
Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary for NY-4 after Nassau Republican Party leadership endorsed her.

priorities.text: Campaign material says she is running to restore the full SALT (state and local tax) deduction, provide additional tax relief for Nassau County families and seniors, support law enforcement, and secure the U.S.-Mexico border.
priorities.quote: Jeanine is running for Congress to build upon her record of protecting Nassau taxpayers. She will continue fighting to lower the tax burden by restoring the full State and Local Tax (SALT) Deduction and providing additional relief for Nassau County families and seniors.

priorities.text: Cites her record as Receiver of Taxes, including holding taxpayer forums to help residents reduce their tax bills, as the basis for her candidacy.
priorities.quote: I have conducted hundreds of taxpayer forums to help people reduce their tax bills.

positions.summary: Supports restoring the full SALT deduction, which would reduce federal tax liability for higher-income households in high-tax states like New York.
Opposes New York's sanctuary-state policy and says she would work with NY Republican members of Congress to undo it and empower local law enforcement on immigration.
positions.quote: Kathy Hochul's Sanctuary State law protects violent criminals instead of law-abiding New Yorkers. ... In Congress, I will work with my colleagues, Homeland Security Committee Chair Andrew Garbarino and Congressman Nick Lalota, to undo New York's sanctuary policies and empower local law enforcement to do their job.

record.text: As Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes since 2020, has held taxpayer forums to help residents understand and reduce their property tax bills.

summary.text: Blay Tarnoff is the Libertarian Party nominee for NY-4 and chairs the Nassau County Libertarian Party. He has worked as a computer systems analyst and holds a law degree. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as not a professional politician and says he opposes socialism.

background.text: Graduated from The American School of Paris, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Brown University in 1980 (an A.B. in mathematics, per the Libertarian Party of New York) and a J.D. from Pace University School of Law in 1996.

According to the Libertarian Party of New York, he spent his career as a computer systems analyst, most recently providing technical support for quantitative financial analysts on Wall Street and developing neural network systems, and presented at NVIDIA GPU Technology Conferences.
Has been a Libertarian activist and party representative since 1990, and currently chairs the Nassau County Libertarian Party and the Libertarian National Judicial Committee.

priorities.text: Says the central problem he would address in Congress is what he calls socialism, and that he would introduce legislation aimed at enforcing constitutional limits against it.
priorities.quote: I will introduce legislation enforcing the Constitution to ELIMINATE socialism in the US.

priorities.text: Says he would work to privatize or eliminate federal administrative agencies, which he views as unconstitutional and as producing waste, and would end inflation by pegging the dollar to gold or bitcoin.
priorities.quote: I will privatize the critical functions of administrative agencies and eliminate them.

priorities.text: Describes his core political philosophy as freedom from government interference in personal, economic, and self-defense decisions.
priorities.quote: I am passionate about the right to be free from harassment by government.

researchNotes: Gillen and Driscoll: as before, neither had completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; their priorities and positions are drawn from campaign-website and social-media statements republished by Ballotpedia. Tarnoff completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey (https://ballotpedia.org/Blay_Tarnoff), which supplied his biography and priorities above; a fact-check removed a `guns` position drawn from a general self-defense/freedom-from-government-interference answer, since it never mentions guns, firearms, or the Second Amendment and does not squarely address gun-law policy, so no positions are recorded for him. No campaign website content beyond the survey was found. Tarnoff and Driscoll have no official government biography; Tarnoff's comes from Ballotpedia and the Libertarian Party of New York, and Driscoll's from Ballotpedia and a News 12 report.
